items.title: Bernie Kirsh interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, August 27, 2022
items.q: The one that I tend to stay with is a guy named Bernie Grundman in Los Angeles. Bernie Grundman Mastering. And he’s a master.

ctx.x: Did you have right people for yourself, like please send it here, don’t send it there?

Yeah. I’ve used a number of different mastering places over the years. The one that I tend to stay with is a guy named Bernie Grundman in Los Angeles. Bernie Grundman Mastering. And he’s a master. All the equipment is tweaked and so forth. You know if you’re mixing in different environments you can — you’re making a determination as

you do by listening and you go okay that sounds good. But how does it compare to other things and is the room accurate and — I think a mastering facility, especially one like that where all kinds of project comes through, becomes a touchstone for what might be considered a reference, a good reference as to what to make changes from . So that’s — there are other technical parts of it as well, in terms of the equipment it goes through before it goes to the plants for manufacturing, but there are lots of things that…
